candidates.exact_span: 4Q3        Lowest four-day average flow rate expected to occur once every three-years
candidates.computation_change_reason: If permit limits or monitoring conditions are keyed to design or critical low-flow statistics, interpreting 4Q3 as the governing flow metric versus another flow basis could change which numeric limits apply and whether flow-conditioned monitoring was required.

candidates.exact_span: BAT        Best available technology economically achievable
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permit limits may be derived from or labeled under BAT; treating a limit as BAT-based versus another technology standard could change which enforceable numeric limit is deemed applicable to a parameter.

candidates.exact_span: BCT        Best conventional pollutant control technology
candidates.computation_change_reason: Limits tied to conventional pollutants and BCT could be selected over BPT or BPJ limits; interpreting the cited technology basis affects which numeric discharge limit applies.

candidates.exact_span: BPT        Best practicable control technology currently available
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of whether a limit is BPT-based can change the applicable enforceable numeric limit when multiple technology-derived limits exist for the same parameter.

The expansion as 'Best management plan' rather than the more common 'Best Management Practice' could change whether referenced BMP obligations are interpreted as plan-submission requirements, operational practices, or monitoring-linked conditions.

candidates.exact_span: BOD        Biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a reported or limited BOD value is the five-day form or another variant affects which numeric limit is comparable and whether a measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: CBOD       Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting CBOD as five-day by default versus another CBOD form changes the applicable limit and compliance comparison when permit text does not explicitly resolve the variant.
What counts as a DMR versus other submittals affects whether monitoring was required and reported, and how missing or non-numeric entries are classified when no ordinary numeric result is present.
If a limit is sourced from ELGs, interpreting this reference determines whether a federal guideline-based numeric limit applies instead of a state- or permit-specific value.

Values reported below MQL or without quantification may not support a numeric exceedance determination and may instead be treated as qualified, non-comparable, or missing evidence rather than ordinary reported results.

candidates.exact_span: mg/l       Milligrams per liter (one part per million)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Unit interpretation is necessary to match reported measurements to permit limits; misalignment on mg/l versus other concentration units would change exceedance calculations.

candidates.exact_span: ug/l       Micrograms per litter (one part per billion)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated ug/l definition and the apparent 'litter' typo could affect unit conversion and whether trace-level measurements are compared against limits expressed in ug/l or another unit.
Reasonable-potential findings can trigger more stringent limits or additional monitoring; interpreting RP status affects whether stricter numeric limits or extra monitoring obligations are in force.
pH limits are expressed in standard units rather than mg/l; applying the wrong unit basis would change whether a reported pH measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

WET is a distinct compliance and monitoring regime with non-conventional numeric endpoints; interpreting results as WET versus conventional chemical parameters changes applicable limits, monitoring requirements, and how absent or non-standard WET results are classified.
Allocations can set or inform discharge limits; interpreting whether a limit is WLA-derived affects which numeric limit applies at a discharge point.
